university: University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences
notes: Single university-layer policy of a health-sciences campus with no computing unit. Section V (clinical) repeats the PHI sentence from Scope and was coded once. Clinical AI is governed by other UAMS policies not coded here. Reconciled from coders A (57 units) and B (56 units); the research-use content (Section III) is mostly outside student coursework. Course layer deferred.

documents.unit: Division of Academic Affairs (Council of Deans, Provost)
documents.title: UAMS Academic Affairs Policy 2.1.6: UAMS Artificial Intelligence Generative Tool Use Policy
documents.stance_why: Section IV.a says GAI use by students 'must be authorized by the course faculty' and that 'Faculty should ... describe the expectations ... whether GAI is prohibited ..., restricted ..., or unrestricted'. The policy sets no default itself beyond requiring instructor permission and hands the choice per course to instructors, with three named tiers, so it delegates.
documents.summary: A campus-wide policy of a health-sciences university covering education, research and administration. It requires instructor authorization for student AI use, with three named levels (prohibited, restricted, unrestricted), plus disclosure, approval of tools by an AI Governance Committee, data and FERPA limits, and annual training. Much of it concerns research and instructor use of AI rather than student coursework.

units.why: The definition says 'Artificial intelligence (AI) is the ability of computer algorithms to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence' and separates mechanical AI from generative AI. It sets what the policy covers, so P61.
units.anchor: Artificial intelligence (AI) is the ability of computer algorithms to perform tasks

units.why: The definition of Generative AI as a tool that can 'generate entire written, audio, synthetic data, or visual works from a prompt', naming code among outputs, fixes the scope of the policy, so P61.

units.why: The definition names the 'AI Governance Committee (AIGC)' as 'responsible for overseeing the governance, approval, monitoring, and lifecycle management of AI tools'. It identifies who owns and enforces the policy, so P80.
units.anchor: responsible for overseeing the governance, approval, monitoring, and lifecycle management of AI tools

units.why: 'Secure' is defined as a tool that 'does not share, transmit, or disclose data outside of UAMS's institutional environment', a definition of a term used in the policy. It is a scope definition (P61) rather than a data rule itself.
units.anchor: does not share, transmit, or disclose data outside of UAMS's institutional environment

units.why: The 'Tool' definition says a model built 'solely as an exercise, assignment, or output of a course' is 'not a Tool' and is exempt from disclosure and approval. This sets scope for student-built AI in courses, so P61, with the course-exercise exemption as the key content.
units.anchor: is not a Tool for purposes of this policy
units.fit_note: Exempts AI systems built as course exercises from disclosure and approval; relevant to computing coursework. (Coder B: Also exempts course-built AI exercises from disclosure and approval, and re-includes them once put to operational use.)
units.resolution_why: A coded actor student and stance permit, B all and neutral. The Tool definition applies to every user and only sets scope (course-built exercises are 'not a Tool for purposes of this policy'), so actor all, stance neutral.

units.why: The sentence says an exercise model that is later used operationally 'becomes a Tool' and 'is subject to disclosure and AI Governance Committee review'. It sets an approval duty for deployed systems, so P65.
units.anchor: it becomes a Tool as of that date
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. The Tool definition ends 'If such a model or system is later put to operational use, it becomes a Tool as of that date and is subject to disclosure and AI Governance Committee review', a real rule separate from the exemption sentence; kept as P65, actor all.

units.why: 'Work' is defined broadly to include 'education, instruction, assessment and evaluation of learners', research, administration and more. This scope definition tells readers what activities the policy covers, so P61.
units.anchor: refers to any UAMS-related non-clinical duties, activities, and outputs

units.why: The text says 'Planned incorporation of AI tools in UAMS environments of education and research should be submitted to the UAMS AI Governance Committee' for review. It is a pre-deployment review duty, so P65.

units.resolution_why: A coded actor instructor, B admin. The passage says 'Planned incorporation of AI tools in UAMS environments of education and research should be submitted' without naming who plans, so actor all.

units.why: The sentence says 'unsafe or inappropriate' tools 'will be blocked on UAMS computers and networks', an institutional control on tools. It is tool vetting by the institution, so P65 (admin actor).

units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B admin. 'AI or GAI tools that are unsafe or inappropriate will be blocked' is an action by UAMS, so admin.

units.why: 'A list of approved AI detection tools and GAI tools ... can be obtained from the UAMS AI Governance Committee' points users to the approved list. That is P92 (know the approved list); the detection-tool mention is incidental.
units.anchor: can be obtained from the UAMS AI Governance Committee

units.why: UAMS 'considers the presentation of AI-generated work as one's own work without appropriate attribution/citation to be plagiarism' and a code-of-conduct violation. It classifies unattributed AI work as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: AI-generated work as one's own work without appropriate attribution/citation to be plagiarism
units.resolution_why: Stance differed (A restrict, B prohibit). Presenting AI work without attribution is plagiarism, but cited AI use is allowed, so the unit restricts rather than prohibits.

units.why: Students 'should refer to each College's policies related to Academic Misconduct' for the grievance process. It points to the formal process owned by colleges, so P81 (procedure), with the referral to college-level policy as the added content.
units.anchor: Students should refer to each College's policies related to Academic Misconduct
units.fit_note: Directs students to college-level integrity and grievance processes rather than prescribing steps. (Coder B: Directs students to the colleges' grievance process rather than telling instructors how to report.)

units.why: Everyone 'must fully disclose how and where they used GAI technology in their work'. A mandatory disclosure of AI use in a submission or work product is P24.
units.anchor: must fully disclose how and where they used GAI technology in their work

units.why: The example says to 'include a statement in the methods or acknowledgements section' of academic writing. It is a disclosure statement under the 'must fully disclose' rule, so P24 (disclose with each submission), should because it is given as an example; P27 does not fit since it is not marking code.
units.anchor: include a statement in the methods or acknowledgements section
units.fit_note: Placement of an AI statement in academic writing (methods or acknowledgements section), not in code; A coded P27, B coded P24.
units.resolution_why: A coded P27 (mark AI-derived code), B coded P24. The example is a disclosure statement in academic writing, not marking code, so P24.

units.why: For educational materials, users 'note in slide footers or syllabi if AI assisted in generating content or images'. It governs disclosure of AI-made course materials, so P48.
units.anchor: note in slide footers or syllabi if AI assisted in generating content or images
units.fit_note: Requires disclosure by noting AI help in footers or syllabi; says nothing about instructor review of the materials. (Coder B: Disclosure placement is given, but no instructor review step.)
units.resolution_why: A coded should, B must. The sentence sits under 'must fully disclose how and where they used GAI'; 'note in slide footers or syllabi' states how, so must.

units.why: Disclosure is not required for 'approved tools, dictation software, language translation, spelling/grammar/punctuation, formatting'. These routine features are exempt from the disclosure rule, so P100.
units.anchor: do not have to disclose the use of GAI with UAMS AI Governance Committee-approved tools
units.fit_note: Also exempts committee-approved tools from disclosure, beyond routine features.

units.why: The policy warns that 'texts and images produced solely by GAI prompts are currently not protected by U.S. copyright law'. A fact about ownership of AI output, so P52.
units.anchor: texts and images produced solely by GAI prompts are

units.anchor: Use of AI-based tools must not violate any copyright or intellectual

units.why: 'Users are responsible for ensuring GAI outputs do not infringe third-party rights' assigns infringement responsibility to the user, a copyright rule, so P52.
units.anchor: Users are responsible for ensuring GAI outputs do not infringe third-party rights
units.resolution_why: Stance differed (A restrict, B neutral). 'Users are responsible for ensuring GAI outputs do not infringe third-party rights' assigns responsibility and takes no position on AI use, so neutral.

units.why: 'GAI work must be checked for accuracy and bias' before use in any document, presentation or assignment. This is a duty to verify output, so P31.
units.anchor: GAI work must be checked for accuracy and bias

units.why: The document 'must be authored by a human' and counts as the user's 'cognitive work'. It says the person owns the submitted work, so P29, with the human-authorship wording as the fit note.
units.anchor: must be authored by a human
units.fit_note: Requires human authorship of the document and says the document is the author's 'cognitive work'; the allowance to incorporate cited GAI information is a separate unit.
units.resolution_why: A and B agree on P29/must. B folded the 'may be incorporated and cited' clause into this unit; it is coded separately here, so this unit covers only the human-authorship rule.

units.why: The sentence allows that 'GAI information may be incorporated and cited' in a scholarly document. It permits AI-derived content under a citation condition, but P16 covers AI-generated code, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: although GAI information may be incorporated and cited
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. 'although GAI information may be incorporated and cited' is a real permission, kept as a separate unit from the human-authorship rule. A coded P16, but P16 covers AI-generated code and this passage is about scholarly documents, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Allows incorporating GAI-derived information into a scholarly or written document when it is cited.

units.why: 'No AI tool is a substitute for human judgement' says humans keep the decision role. It is the principle that AI must not replace thinking, so P32.

units.fit_note: Applies to researchers evaluating AI recommendations, not student coursework.
units.resolution_why: A coded modality informs, B must. 'No AI tool is a substitute for human judgement' is a principle, so informs; the duty that follows is coded in its own unit.

units.why: Researchers 'must evaluate the accuracy and appropriateness of recommendations made by AI tools and make the final determination'. It is a verify-output duty (P31) for research.
units.anchor: must evaluate the accuracy and appropriateness of recommendations made by AI tools
units.fit_note: Applies to researchers and students in research; adds that the human makes the final determination.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. 'Researchers and students involved in research must evaluate the accuracy and appropriateness of recommendations made by AI tools and make the final determination' is a verification duty distinct from the principle sentence; kept as P31.

units.why: 'Investigators must describe in their human subject research submissions to the IRB any use of AI'. It is a research-specific AI rule tied to IRB review, so P62.
units.anchor: Investigators must describe in their human subject research submissions to the IRB
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B instructor. 'Investigators' are researchers, not instructors, so actor all.

units.why: Use of AI where 'inputs will leave the UAMS environment' or outputs could 're-identify research participants' 'must be described in IRB submissions', and the IRB decides the extent of consent description. This is a research AI rule deferring to IRB, so P62.
units.anchor: must be described in IRB submissions
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. 'Use of AI, particularly when inputs will leave the UAMS environment, and/or outputs could potentially re-identify research participants, must be described in IRB submissions' adds a second disclosure trigger beyond the first sentence; kept as P62.

units.why: 'The UAMS IRB will make the final determination of the extent of the AI description in the consent process' defers to the IRB for research, P62.
units.anchor: The UAMS IRB will make the final determination of the extent of the AI description
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. 'The UAMS IRB will make the final determination of the extent of the AI description in the consent process' names who decides, a real research-governance statement; kept as P62.

units.why: Investigators unsure whether their AI use falls within the description 'should consult the AI Governance Committee or IT Security prior to submission'. It tells people to ask before acting when unsure, so P10.
units.anchor: should consult the AI Governance Committee or IT Security prior to submission
units.fit_note: Addressed to investigators and sends them to the committee or IT Security, not to an instructor. (Coder B: Addressed to research investigators who consult a committee, not students asking instructors.)
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B instructor. Addressed to investigators, so all.

units.why: 'Any use of external AI tools involving Study Data requires prior Institutional Review Board (IRB) review and approval'. A research AI rule deferring to IRB, so P62.
units.anchor: requires prior Institutional Review Board (IRB) review and approval
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B instructor. 'Any use of external AI tools involving Study Data requires prior IRB review' binds any user, so all.

units.why: 'AI tools must be assessed by Investigators for potential bias' is a research duty about bias in AI tools; bias concerns are P53 but this is a research procedure, so P62 fits better.
units.anchor: AI tools must be assessed by Investigators for potential bias
units.fit_note: Concerns assessing the tool for bias in research datasets rather than verifying one output.
units.resolution_why: A coded P62, B P31. The sentence asks investigators to assess tools for bias in research datasets, not to verify one output, so P62 (research governance) fits; B's own fit note says P31 fits only partly.

units.why: 'Investigators must maintain a record of AI tool versions, prompts, outputs, and decision rationales in the research file' is a duty to keep AI logs, so P26 (keep logs), addressed to investigators (all) while working.
units.anchor: must maintain a record of AI tool versions, prompts, outputs, and decision rationales
units.fit_note: Records are kept in the research file, not submitted with a student assignment; B coded P62 with the same note.
units.resolution_why: A coded P26, B P62. 'Investigators must maintain a record of AI tool versions, prompts, outputs, and decision rationales' is a duty to keep AI logs, which is what P26 covers; actor is investigators, so all.

units.why: The IRB 'shall follow ... periodic review of AI use in active studies to ensure compliance with evolving standards'. It is an institutional review cycle for research AI, so P62.
units.anchor: periodic review of AI use in active studies

units.why: 'Inputting identifiable participant data into public or non-secure AI tools is prohibited' is a flat ban on a data input, so P50.
units.anchor: Inputting identifiable participant data into public or non-secure AI tools is prohibited.

units.why: 'Any use of a Tool ... must be reviewed and approved by the AI in Research Committee'. Approval of tools before use, so P65; the registry clause is a separate P98 unit.
units.anchor: must be reviewed and approved by the AI in Research Committee
units.resolution_why: A coded P65 (with registry in the fit note), B P98 on the registry clause. The sentence holds two rules, review-and-approval (P65) and reporting to the AI Tool Registry (P98); they are split into two units. Actor is any user of a Tool, so all; phase before-course because approval precedes use.

units.why: Tools 'must be reviewed and approved by the AI in Research Committee, and reported to the AI Governance Committee for inclusion in the AI Tool Registry': a registry documenting deployed tools, P98.
units.anchor: reported to the AI Governance Committee for inclusion in the AI Tool Registry
units.fit_note: Combines reporting of research Tools to the AI Governance Committee with entry in the AI Tool Registry.
units.resolution_why: Split from the A36/B35 sentence. 'reported to the AI Governance Committee for inclusion in the AI Tool Registry' is a documentation duty separate from approval, so P98; actor all (any user of a Tool).

units.why: 'Denials or disputes may be appealed to the AI Governance Committee' sets the route for challenging a review decision, which is a process for exceptions and disputes, so P80.
units.anchor: Denials or disputes may be appealed to the AI Governance Committee.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase general, B when-misuse. Appeals of denials concern the review decision, not misuse, so general.

units.why: 'Use of GAI by students to satisfy course requirements must be authorized by the course faculty, trainer, or education supervisor.' The instructor decides whether students may use AI, so P04 (instructor sets the rule); the next sentence carries the fallback rule (P06).
units.anchor: must be authorized by the course faculty, trainer, or education supervisor
units.fit_note: Stated as a default rule for the whole university rather than for a silent syllabus.
units.resolution_why: A coded P04, B P06 (and phase course-start). 'Use of GAI by students ... must be authorized by the course faculty' makes the instructor decide whether AI is allowed, so P04. The default-when-silent point is coded on the next sentence. Phase during-work, as it governs use of GAI to satisfy course requirements.

units.why: Use 'must be specifically allowed by the instructor/mentor for the given course or activity'. Unless allowed, AI is off, which is a fallback default (P06); P04 is already coded on the preceding sentence and does not state the default.
units.anchor: must be specifically allowed by the instructor/mentor for the given course or activity
units.fit_note: Sets the default as not allowed unless the instructor allows it, per course or activity. (Coder B: Permission is activity-specific; does not say outright that rules do not carry over.)
units.resolution_why: A coded P06, B P11. 'must be specifically allowed by the instructor/mentor for the given course or activity' means AI is off unless allowed, a fallback rule (P06). The per-course scope is part of the same sentence and noted in the fit note; P11 states that permissions do not carry over, which the passage does not say.

units.why: 'Faculty should make a clear, conscious effort to describe the expectations for a given course/activity'. This asks instructors to communicate AI expectations, so P09.
units.anchor: Faculty should make a clear, conscious effort to describe the expectations

units.why: The policy defines three categories: 'prohibited', 'restricted' and 'unrestricted' use of GAI per course or activity. Named levels, so P05.
units.anchor: prohibited (i.e., not allowed in any capacity), restricted

units.why: Violating the policy or the instructor's stated expectations 'might be considered a violation of the College's Academic Misconduct Policy'. That classifies misuse as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: might be considered a violation of the College's Academic Misconduct Policy
units.resolution_why: Stance differed (A restrict, B prohibit). Violation 'might be considered' misconduct; unauthorized use is sanctionable but AI is not banned outright, so restrict.

units.why: The sanction 'could include disciplinary action up to and including dismissal' states the possible penalty. It names a ceiling but not a fixed penalty per offense, so P37 with a note.
units.anchor: disciplinary action up to and including dismissal
units.fit_note: Gives only a range of possible action up to dismissal, no concrete penalty per offense. (Coder B: Gives only a ceiling (dismissal), not set penalties by offense.)
units.resolution_why: Stance differed (A restrict, B prohibit). 'could include disciplinary action up to and including dismissal' states a ceiling for violations of a delegated rule, so restrict.

units.why: 'Instructors may have additional requirements regarding citation or acknowledgement of the use of GAI in assignments' lets instructors set extra rules, so P04, actor instructor, modality may; the disclosure content is noted in the fit note.
units.anchor: Instructors may have additional requirements regarding citation or acknowledgement
units.fit_note: Lets instructors add citation and acknowledgement requirements beyond the policy's own, so it concerns disclosure as well as instructor discretion.
units.resolution_why: A coded P24/student/informs, B P04/instructor/may. 'Instructors may have additional requirements regarding citation or acknowledgement' empowers instructors to set extra rules, so P04, actor instructor, modality may, no stance of its own.

units.why: Instructors 'may not input any student-identifiable information or student work into GAI, plagiarism checking tools, or AI-detection software without explicit written permission from the student unless approved for use by UAMS'. This is a FERPA data-protection rule, so P50.
units.anchor: instructors may not input any student-identifiable information or student work into GAI
units.fit_note: Binds instructors (not students) and covers plagiarism checkers and AI detectors as well as GAI. (Coder B: Binds instructors; covers student work and detectors.)

units.why: 'AI detection software currently available is inaccurate and unreliable' says detectors cannot be trusted, so P39.
units.anchor: AI detection software currently available is inaccurate and unreliable.

units.why: 'Instructors are prohibited from asking Students for permission to input their work into GAI without express permission from the UAMS AI Governance Committee.' A data and consent limit on instructors, so P50.
units.anchor: Instructors are prohibited from asking Students for permission to input their work
units.fit_note: Restricts how instructors ask students for consent.
units.resolution_why: Stance differed (A restrict, B prohibit). The ban is conditional on committee permission ('without express permission from the UAMS AI Governance Committee'), so restrict.

units.why: 'Approval from the UAMS AI Governance Committee is also required for centralized tracking of licensure and any potential integration into other systems like Blackboard.' This is committee review of tools, so P65.
units.anchor: Approval from the UAMS AI Governance Committee is also required for centralized tracking of licensure

units.why: 'Any use of GAI by instructors to assist or review grading or evaluating student class assignments or work requires prior approval' from the committee. AI-assisted grading allowed only through an approval chain, so P101.
units.anchor: any use of GAI by instructors to assist or review grading or evaluating student class
units.resolution_why: Same type in both (P101). Anchor taken from B because it names the grading use.

units.why: 'Any use of GAI to analyze student grades or other records also requires prior approval by the appropriate Dean and the UAMS AI Governance Committee' binds instructors with an approval condition on AI use with student records; it is the nearest fit to P101 (conditions for AI-assisted grading), must, restrict.
units.anchor: analyze student grades or other records also requires prior approval
units.fit_note: Covers analysis of student grades or other records, not only grading; needs approval from the Dean and the AI Governance Committee.
units.resolution_why: A coded UNCOVERED, B P101. The sentence is the next conditional approval in the grading and student-records chain ('Any use of GAI to analyze student grades or other records also requires prior approval'), close enough to P101 with a fit note.

units.why: AI-related disclosures or violations 'must be reported within 24 hours to the UAMS AI Governance Committee' and other offices. A duty to report incidents, so P71.
units.anchor: must be reported within 24 hours to the UAMS AI Governance Committee
units.resolution_why: Stance differed (A restrict, B neutral). Reporting within 24 hours is a procedure that takes no position on AI use, so neutral.

units.why: 'All faculty, staff, and students will be required to take annual AI and GAI training.' Mandatory AI training for the whole community, so P70.
units.anchor: all faculty, staff, and students will be required to take annual AI and GAI training
units.resolution_why: Stance differed (A neutral, B require). Annual training is required, but training is not AI use being required in coursework, so neutral.

units.why: The reference notes Arkansas law 'Requires all public entities in Arkansas, including UAMS, to adopt formal policies governing the authorized use of AI'. It ties the policy to state law, so P77.
units.anchor: Requires all public entities in Arkansas, including UAMS, to adopt formal policies

units.why: The law requires 'a human employee or designee retain final decision-making authority' over automated decision tools. This keeps humans responsible for decisions, so P73.
units.anchor: a human employee or designee retain final decision-making authority
